questions.q: In MS Word, bold, italic and underline buttons are found in the Font group of which tab?
questions.solution: Character formatting lives in the **Font group of the Home tab**. Insert adds objects, View changes views, Layout handles page setup.

questions.q: Which shortcut inserts **today's date** into the active cell?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+;** stamps the date; **Ctrl+Shift+;** stamps the current time.

questions.q: Which OSI layer sits DIRECTLY above the Transport layer?
questions.solution: Order above Transport: **Session (5), Presentation (6), Application (7)**.

questions.q: Receiving a file from a web server to your computer is called:
questions.solution: Downloading copies data from the server down to your device; uploading sends it the other way; streaming plays without saving the whole file.
questions.shortcut: Down to you = download; up to the server = upload.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Succeeded**: succeed is one of the three -ceed verbs (proceed, succeed, exceed), so it keeps **-ceed** before -ed. It also has double c.

questions.q:
Select the word which is most opposite in meaning to the given word.

VIRTUE
questions.solution: *Virtue* = moral goodness → its standard opposite is **vice** (moral fault). 'Value' drifts to worth, and the v-initial 'virtuosity/vigour' are shape decoys.
questions.shortcut: Kill the v-initial decoys; pick the genuine moral opposite.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
questions.solution: Subjects ending in -ics (mathematics, physics, economics) take a singular verb → **is**.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom in bold.

Meena was **on cloud nine** when she cleared the exam.
questions.solution: Clearing an exam is good news, so the meaning must be positive. *On cloud nine* = **extremely happy**.
questions.shortcut: Good-news sentence → pick the only happy option.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true about Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)?
options: They are registered under Section 45-IA of the RBI Act, 1934
They can lend and make investments
They can issue cheques to their customers
DICGC insurance does not cover their deposits
questions.solution: NBFCs **cannot issue cheques** because they lie outside the payment and settlement system. The other statements are true: registration under Section 45-IA, lending rights, and no DICGC cover.
questions.shortcut: The NBFC's three 'noes': no demand deposits, no cheques, no DICGC.

questions.q: **Vinegar** is a solution of about 5–8% —
questions.solution: Vinegar = dilute **acetic acid (CH₃COOH)**, made by fermenting ethanol. Citric acid is lemon's; formic acid is the ant sting's.

questions.q: India's first biosphere reserve, set up in 1986, is:
questions.solution: The **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve** (1986) spans Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka at the junction of the Western and Eastern Ghats. Gulf of Mannar and Nanda Devi came in the later lists.

questions.q: The song ***Vande Mataram*** occurs in Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel —
questions.solution: ***Anandamath* (1882)** contains Vande Mataram; Tagore first sang it at the **1896 Calcutta session** of the Congress.

questions.q: The value of $\sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta$ is:
questions.solution:
Cube the identity: $(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)^3 = 1$ expands to

$\sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta + 3\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = 1$, so the sum is $1 - 3\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta$.
questions.shortcut: $x^3 + y^3 = (x+y)^3 - 3xy(x+y)$ with $x+y = 1$. Trap: $1 - 2s^2c^2$ — that is the FOURTH-power form.

questions.q: If the six-digit number 6x52y4 is divisible by 72, what is the value of x + y?
questions.solution:
$72 = 8 \times 9$.
**Rule of 8:** $2y4$ must be divisible by 8 → 224 or 264 → $y = 2$ or $y = 6$.
**Rule of 9:** digit sum $6 + x + 5 + 2 + y + 4 = 17 + x + y$ must be a multiple of 9 → $x + y = 1$ or $10$.
- $y = 2$: $x + y$ cannot be 1, so $x + y = 10$ → $x = 8$ (685224 ✓).
- $y = 6$: $x + y = 10$ → $x = 4$ (645264 ✓).
In both cases $x + y = 10$.
questions.shortcut: Digit sum 17 + (x + y) must reach 27 because y ≥ 2 rules out x + y = 1. So x + y = 10.

questions.q: Three numbers in GP have a product of 64 and a sum of 21. The numbers are:
questions.solution:
$a^3 = 64$, so $a = 4$.
$\dfrac{4}{r} + 4 + 4r = 21 \Rightarrow 4r^2 - 17r + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow r = 4$.
Numbers: 1, 4, 16.
questions.shortcut: Option check: only 1, 4, 16 has product 64 and sum 21.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has equal sides of $10$ cm and base $12$ cm. Its area is:
questions.solution:
$h = \sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{64} = 8$ cm (6-8-10 halves).

$K = \frac12 \times 12 \times 8 = 48$ sq cm.

questions.q:
**Statement:** The government will give free cooking-gas connections to poor families to reduce smoke inside homes.

**Assumptions:**
I. Some poor families use fuels that produce smoke while cooking.
II. Every poor family will stop using firewood completely.

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
options: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.solution: Negate I: no poor family uses smoky fuel — the scheme has no purpose, so I is **implicit**. II expects a complete change by every family; some reduction is enough reason for the scheme — **not implicit**. Answer: **only I**.
questions.shortcut: Total words — every, completely — mark the trap.

questions.q: Select the related word: **Hygrometer : Humidity :: Ammeter : ?**
questions.solution: A hygrometer measures humidity, so the link is instrument : quantity measured. An **ammeter measures current**. Voltage goes with a voltmeter and resistance with an ohmmeter; 'electricity' is too vague.

questions.q: **P is the husband of Q. R is the father of P.** How is **R related to Q**?
questions.solution: P and Q are married; R is P's father. One marriage crossing from 'father' → R is Q's **father-in-law**.
questions.shortcut: Husband's father = father-in-law; every marriage line adds '-in-law'.

questions.q:
**Statement:** Notice in a housing society: 'The overhead water tank will be cleaned on Sunday from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Residents are requested to store water in advance.'

**Assumptions:**
I. Residents will read the notice before Sunday.
II. Cleaning the tank will take a whole week.

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
options: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.solution: Negate I: nobody reads it in time — the notice is useless, so I is **implicit**. II contradicts the notice, which gives a four-hour window — **not implicit**. Answer: **only I**.
questions.shortcut: An assumption that contradicts the statement can never be implicit.
